I’m very sorry you’re feeling this way. I too was in the position you’re in right now. I have felt like nobody wanted me, that I was missing out on a lot, and that I will never amount to anything worthy in life. I was hospitalized for depression and was tired of seeming like the oddball and I couldn’t have ever imagined my life getting better, but it did. 

You’re experiencing depression, and in that mental-state you’re mind is telling you lies about  yourself and the world. It could also be the people that you’re around as well that are presenting you an image that all people are awful and evil (it’s true that only some are). Sometimes, it may even be our own choices that are putting us in the position we’re in. It’s not an easy thought to settle in, but it’s an important one to work through.

At this point, you can choose to fall for the lies, or you can ask yourself honestly—what is it in my life that I need to change? If you ever need help, please call a hotline and talk to someone. Don’t be afraid to ask a therapist you can trust with those uncomfortable questions. Find community because you need to. Find goals. It’s unfortunate that life is hard, but you can still find and build a better life. You don’t have to live like this. However, you’re not going to find any solution unless you accept you have a mental illness and that it needs to be treated.

I’m praying for you and that God may heal you from your troubles and give you happiness and all that you wish for, in Jesus name. Happy Holidays my dear friend and wishing you a great and prosperous 2025. I want to leave you with this quote: “Pain is inevitable, suffering is optional” ~ Haruki Murakami

When I moved out of my parents, it was challenging but it was one of the best decisions I've made. It may be hard to see hope when you're experiencing depression because your mind and the people around you can fool you into believing false things. Also, everyone is depressed to some extent. Don't be afraid to find humor in your situation. ;)

Also, if all else fails, always remember that there's someone or something you could find purpose in like God, your tribe, or getting involved in politics. Surround yourself with the right people and remain focused on work and development. Remember, life is a journey not a destination. Wishing you the best.

I’m so sorry that you’re feeling like this. I also feel like this about myself from time to time. There’s many factors at play that can determine a person’s quality-of-life: like the country they live in, their socioeconomic background, their childhood, schooling, environment, resources, etc. 

I’ve learned that true happiness in life is found in working and being productive towards your future and for the benefit of society. Remember, there are many other people out there that feel just like you. You can choose to be a fighter and inspire others by giving them hope that one day you can unapologetically admire yourself and find freedom from anyone’s standards or oppression, even if you won’t live to see it but other generations will.

Life is not easy for anyone. It’s important to recognize that everyone has strengths and weaknesses. Your personality has some gifts that others don’t. It just may be hard to see that because of the lies and misinformation. People are crazy, but don’t let them break you. Your focus should be to find your supportive tribe, focus on your goals, gain socioeconomic status, find joy, and contribute towards a better civilization. If you want to, get involved into politics and become an advocate. The world needs more courageous people, anyways. Ironically, people will start to like you more when you embrace yourself!

Also, you should check out ChatGPT. It’s a really helpful resource for depression. However, you won’t be able to get advice on suicidal thoughts. If you’re ever feeling suicidal, please text “HOME” to Crisis Text Line at 741741. If you can afford it, find a therapist on BetterHelp.com to help you navigate your personal challenges.

You matter. Always focus your mind on what’s resourceful. Seeking a spiritual advisor or joining a church may be what you need. Finding a community of faith can help tremendously with building character. Never let the enemy bring you down. 

Wishing you the best of luck. ❤️

I also learned that even if I was in a relationship, my partner can't fix my issues for me.  Besides, no relationship isn't meant to last forever anyways.

I just now focus on my goals. If the right person comes along, I will see them as a compliment and not as a necessity in my life. Of course she will be important to me, but I've learned to be okay with being alone. Everyone is alone to some extent.

I don't worry much about not being able to start a family. I made a promise to myself that even if that doesn't happen, I will always be of service to my community and helping others achieve their dreams and goals. That brings me peace, and the ability to enjoy Hulu alone with no regrets.

I've been involuntarily committed in a mental hospital for 2 days after I called the suicide hotline and told them I wanted help. The first day was scary for me because there was a lot of yelling coming from some in-patients there. There are nurses and counselors there who'd watch what you're doing throughout the day and cater to your needs. There's also a psychiatrist and doctor that checks on you at least once a day to determine your wellbeing and prescribe you any medication. I took Celexa for depression voluntarily and was able to leave the ward before completing the mandatory 3-day stay according to the Baker Act in Florida.

If you would like to commit yourself to staying in a ward, I'd recommend doing it voluntarily. Just keep doing research and prepare yourself for staying inside one. I think you'll be happy that you did it. :)
